title: Cold Soba Noodle Salad with Edamame and Sesame Dressing
summary: A refreshing Japanese-inspired lunch with chilled soba noodles, tender edamame, crisp vegetables and a nutty sesame-tamari dressing. It is bright, savoury and ideal for warm days or make-ahead lunches.
steps: Bring a large pan of water to the boil. Add the soba noodles and cook according to the packet instructions, usually 4–6 minutes, until just tender but still springy.
Add the edamame for the final 2 minutes of cooking, then drain everything and rinse thoroughly under cold running water until completely cool. Drain well so the dressing does not become watery.
Whisk the tamari, rice vinegar, sesame oil, maple syrup, grated ginger, lime juice and a pinch of salt together in a large bowl until glossy and combined.
Add the cold noodles, edamame, cucumber, carrot, spring onions and coriander to the dressing. Toss gently with tongs until the noodles are evenly coated and the vegetables are distributed.
Divide between bowls and scatter with sesame seeds. Serve cold, or chill for up to 24 hours and toss again before eating.
